words.gloss: siddhabasti (a named enema, lit. 'proven enema'); preparation (kalpa)

hindi: अब इसलिए हम सिद्धबस्ति-कल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparation (kalpa) of the siddhabasti (a named enema; lit. 'proven enema').
notes: Chapter-opening formula. Printed 'athātaḥ' is read atha + ataḥ with the visarga kept. basti = enema (vasti normalised to basti).

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (as printed); agreement uncertain
dvandva, first members of a compound ending in karān in the next token

hindi: सिद्धबस्तियों का सब देहधारियों के लिए सदा प्रयोग करे। ये बिना विपत्ति के, बहुत फलों वाले, बल और बुद्धि उत्पन्न करने वाले तथा सुखद हैं।
english: One should always employ siddhabastis (the named enemas) for all embodied beings. (They are) free from mishap, of many benefits, producing strength and intelligence, and pleasant.

text_flags.why: possible: v for b (n+b is regularly written nb); 'bala' (strength) fits the sense
possible: the other adjectives are accusative plural and agree with the siddhabastis of 2; 'nirvyāpadaḥ' (nominative singular) does not agree

notes:
line 05.05.2: Genitive 'sarvadehinām' is rendered 'for all embodied beings'; a literal alternative is 'of all embodied beings'.
line 05.05.3: Continues 2 (adjectives of the siddhabastis). The compound 'bala-buddhi-karān' runs across the token break. The Hindi and English supply 'they are' only as the copula the construction needs; the text has no verb.

words.gloss: miśi (dill, Anethum sowa; disputed: fennel, Foeniculum vulgare, also given)
castor (eraṇḍa, Ricinus communis; standard); root; decoction

hindi: मधु और तैल बराबर; कर्ष; सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से दो पिचु; मिशि यानी सम्भवतः सोया। एरण्ड यानी अरंडी की जड़ के काढ़े से मधु और तैल वाला निरूह यानी काढ़े की बस्ति।
english: Honey and oil, equal; a karṣa (a unit of weight); from rock salt (saindhava), two picu (a unit of weight); miśi (probably dill). The nirūha (decoction enema) made with a decoction of the root of eraṇḍa (castor), with honey and oil.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kāthena' lacks the v of kvātha (decoction); sense and parallels in the chapter point to kvātha

notes:
line 05.05.4: Elliptic list of quantities with no verb; the exact relation of 'karṣaḥ' and 'saindhavāt dvipicuḥ' to the ingredients is not clear from the line (possible reading (source not checked): one karṣa of rock salt, two picu of miśi; not applied here). Identifications: saindhava = rock salt (standard); miśi = dill, Anethum sowa (disputed; fennel also proposed).
line 05.05.5: No verb in the line; it names the enema. Identification: eraṇḍa = Ricinus communis (standard).
OPEN (05.05.5) [minor] notes / mādhutailikaḥ: mādhutailika is a known named nirūha (honey-oil); 'made with honey and oil' in English plus 'with honey and oil' repeats; observation only. Suggested: note that mādhutailika is likely a proper name of this nirūha (probable)

words.gloss: prameha (a group of urinary disorders, linked with diabetes; probable); arśas (haemorrhoids, piles; standard)
words.gram: dvandva, first members of the compound

words.gloss: worms; gulma (abdominal lump); intestine; enlargement; dispelling
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, m. nom. sg.; antravṛddhi = intestinal hernia (standard)
tat-puruṣa, m. nom. sg.; raktapitta = bleeding from upper or lower passages (probable)

hindi: यह रसायन है, तथा प्रमेह यानी मूत्र-विकार, अर्श यानी बवासीर, कृमि यानी कीड़े, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ और अन्त्रवृद्धि यानी आँत उतरना या हर्निया को दूर करने वाला है। और यष्टीमधु यानी मुलेठी के साथ, आँखों के लिए हितकर तथा रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव वाले विकार को जीतने वाला।
english: It is rejuvenating (rasāyana) and dispels prameha (a group of urinary disorders), arśas (haemorrhoids), worms, gulma (abdominal lump) and antravṛddhi (intestinal hernia). And with licorice (yaṣṭīmadhu), good for the eyes, conquering raktapitta (a bleeding disorder).
notes:
line 05.05.6: Continues 5; the adjectives agree with nirūhaḥ. 'pramehārśaḥ' read as prameha-arśaḥ (sandhi a+a). Identifications: arśas = haemorrhoids (standard); prameha = urinary disorders, commonly linked with diabetes (probable); antravṛddhi = hernia (standard). Review: 'rasāyanam' is neuter, a predicate ('it is a rasāyana'), not an adjective agreeing with nirūhaḥ. The printed visarga of 'pramehārśaḥ' sits where a compound member (prameha-arśa-) would have none; it may be a print error, or arśaḥ is a separate word; the reading as a list of objects of -nut is kept.
line 05.05.7: Continues 5-6 (the nirūha with licorice added). Identification: yaṣṭīmadhu = Glycyrrhiza glabra (standard); raktapitta = a bleeding disorder, lit. 'blood-pitta' (probable).

words.gram: dvandva + -vat (possessive suffix), m. nom. sg.; ājya = ghee

words.gloss: anus; knee; thigh; pṛṣṭaśaṇa (unclear: printed form, probably pṛṣṭha 'back' + śroṇi 'hip' on a conjectural reading); bladder region; penis (mehana)
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, first members of a compound ending in śūlajit

hindi: यापन, गाढ़े कल्क से युक्त तथा मधु, तैल, वसा यानी चर्बी और घी वाला। यह गुदा, घुटने, जाँघ, एक अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार पीठ और कूल्हे, मूत्राशय और लिंग की पीड़ा को जीतने वाला है।
english: The yāpana (sustaining enema), with a thick paste, and having honey, oil, fat (vasā) and ghee. It conquers pain in the anus, knee, thigh, back and hip (on a conjectural reading of the damaged word), bladder region and penis (mehana).

text_flags.why: possible: 'pṛṣṭaśaṇa' is not a word; 'pṛṣṭha-śroṇi' (back, hip) fits a list of body parts; the final -a of mehana before śūlajit is also doubtful (mehana-śūlajit)

notes:
line 05.05.8: No verb. 'ghana-kalka' = thick paste of drugs. 'madhutailavasājyavān' read as madhu-taila-vasā-ājya + vat (having).
line 05.05.9: The compound 'pāyu...mehana-śūlajit' is read as 'conquering pain of anus, knee, ... penis'. The middle of the compound is doubtful, so the translation of 'back and hip' is conjectural. Continues 8.

words.gloss: rock salt (saindhava); half; akṣa (a unit of weight)
hapuṣā (juniper berries, Juniperus communis; probable); half; pala (a unit of weight)

hindi: प्रसृत के भागों से, घी, शहद, वसा यानी चर्बी और तैल के साथ तैयार करे। यापन, आधे अक्ष सैन्धव और आधे पल हपुषा यानी सम्भवतः हाऊबेर से युक्त।
english: One should prepare, with prasṛta-portions (prasṛta, a handful measure), with ghee, honey, fat (vasā) and oil. The yāpana (sustaining enema), accompanied by half an akṣa (a unit of weight) of rock salt (saindhava) and half a pala (a unit of weight) of hapuṣā (probably juniper berries).
notes:
line 05.05.10: Instrumental plural of the four substances; 'prasṛta' is a measure (about two palas in the standard tables).
line 05.05.11: Printed 'arddha' normalised to ardha (doubled dd). The division of the compound into 'half akṣa of saindhava' and 'half pala of hapuṣā' is the natural reading but the line has no separating word. hapuṣā = Juniperus communis (probable).

words.gloss: with vacā (sweet flag, Acorus calamus; standard); pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard)

words.gram: last member of the bahuvrīhi sa-vacā-pippalī-phalaḥ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: एरण्ड की जड़ का काढ़ा, शहद, तैल, सैन्धव के साथ। यह युक्तरथ बस्ति है, वचा यानी बच, पिप्पली यानी पीपर और फल के साथ।
english: A decoction of the root of eraṇḍa (castor), honey, oil, with rock salt (saindhava). This is the yuktaratha enema (basti), with vacā (sweet flag), pippalī (long pepper) and fruit (phala).

text_flags.why: possible: 'niḥkkātha' for niḥkvātha (decoction); the doubled k and missing v are probably print errors

notes:
line 05.05.12: A list of ingredients with no verb; it continues the description of the yāpana of 11.
line 05.05.13: 'savacāpippalī phalaḥ' is read sa-vacā-pippalī-phalaḥ; the fruit (phala) is not named further and might also be read as 'pippalī fruit'. The printed space after 'savacāpippalī' is kept in src. Identifications: vacā = Acorus calamus (standard); pippalī = Piper longum (standard).

lines_deva: सकाथो मधु पैंढुंथा शताव्हा हिंगु सैंधवं
सुरदारु च रास्ना च बस्तिदोषहरः शिवः
lines_iast: sakātho madhu paiṃḍhuṃthā śatāvhā hiṃgu saiṃdhavaṃ
suradāru ca rāsnā ca bastidoṣaharaḥ śivaḥ

words.gloss: suradāru (devadāru, Himalayan cedar, Cedrus deodara; standard)
rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata; disputed, Alpinia galanga also given)

hindi: काढ़े के साथ, शहद, पैण्डुण्ठा, जो छपा हुआ अस्पष्ट शब्द है और अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार लिया गया है, शताह्वा यानी सम्भवतः सोया, हींग और सैन्धव। सुरदारु यानी देवदार और रास्ना, जिसकी पहचान में मतभेद है; यह बस्ति के दोषों को हरने वाला और कल्याणकारी है।
english: With a decoction, honey, paiṃḍhuṃthā (on a conjectural reading; the printed word is unclear), śatāhvā (probably dill), asafoetida (hiṅgu) and rock salt (saindhava). Suradāru (devadāru, deodar cedar) and rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata), removing the faults of the enema (basti-doṣa), auspicious.

text_flags.why: possible: kvātha (decoction) with v dropped
possible: letters transposed; śatāhvā is the usual word
the printed word is not a known drug name; possibly a name beginning pi- (e.g. a corrupt form of a drug name), kept unsplit and unglossed

notes:
line 05.05.14: List of ingredients with no verb. 'paiṃḍhuṃthā' is damaged or corrupt in print and is not interpreted. śatāhvā = Anethum sowa, dill (probable; fennel also proposed).
OPEN (05.05.14) [minor] text_flags / paiṃḍhuṃthā: Needs a human: the print is metrically a 3-syllable word (line = 16 syllables), so a 3-syllable drug name is expected; left unsplit and unidentified, which is right. Suggested: (no change)
OPEN (05.05.14) proofread pass, unsure: 'पैंढुंथा' looks garbled but the intended herb is not certain.
line 05.05.15: 'bastidoṣa' is read as faults (defects or ill effects) of the enema. The line continues the list begun in 12-14; the adjectives apply to the whole preparation. Identifications: suradāru = Cedrus deodara (standard); rāsnā = Pluchea lanceolata (disputed; Alpinia galanga also proposed).

words.gloss: five; roots; pañcamūla (a group of five roots; which group is not stated)
māgadhikā (long pepper, Piper longum; standard synonym of pippalī)

hindi: पंचमूल का काढ़ा, तैल, मागधिका यानी पिप्पली और शहद। सैन्धव और मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी सहित यह सिद्धबस्ति कहा गया है।
english: A decoction of the pañcamūla (the group of five roots), oil, māgadhikā (long pepper) and honey. With rock salt (saindhava) and madhuka (probably licorice), it is called the siddhabasti.

text_flags.why: possible: 'niḥkkātha' for niḥkvātha (decoction); the visarga + t- sandhi (niḥkvāthaḥ + tailam -> niḥkvāthastailam) is regular

notes:
line 05.05.16: Ingredient list with no verb. Which pañcamūla (the lesser or the greater five) is not stated here.
line 05.05.17: 'samadhukaḥ' could also be read sa-madhu-kaḥ ('with honey'), but honey is already named in 16, so madhuka (licorice, probable) is taken.

words.gloss: two; pañcamūla (double five-root group, i.e. ten roots)
pāṭhā (probably Cissampelos pareira; probable); vatsaka (kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica; probable); toyada (musta, Cyperus rotundus; probable; lit. 'water-giver')

hindi: द्विपंचमूल, त्रिफला, फल और बिल्व यानी बेल को पकाए। गोमूत्र में, उससे, तथा पाठा, वत्सक यानी सम्भवतः कुटज और तोयद यानी सम्भवतः नागरमोथा के पिसे हुए के साथ।
english: One should cook the dvipañcamūla (the double five-root group, ten roots), triphalā (the three fruits), fruit (phala) and bilva (bael). In cow's urine, by that, and with the ground (ones) of pāṭhā (probably Cissampelos pareira), vatsaka (probably kuṭaja) and toyada (probably musta).

text_flags.why: possible: 'tenai' is not a form; 'tena' (by that) fits sense and metre

notes:
line 05.05.18: Printed 'vilva' normalised to bilva. The compound is read as a list of four; 'phala' is not specified and may belong to the preceding word. bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard). Continues in 19.
line 05.05.19: Continues 18 (verb pācayet carried over); no verb in this line. Identifications: pāṭhā = Cissampelos pareira (probable); vatsaka = Holarrhena antidysenterica, kuṭaja (probable); toyada = Cyperus rotundus, musta (probable).
OPEN (05.05.19) [minor] text_flags / tenai: Reading of 'tenai' is not secure: 'tena' (by that) leaves the construction unclear (what is 'that'?). Metre does not decide (te-nai and te-na are both two syllables). Human decision. Suggested: (no change)

words.gloss: pāṇḍu (pale); disease; the disease pāṇḍu, anaemia with pallor (standard)
visūcī (acute vomiting and purging, cholera-like illness; probable)

hindi: फलों सहित, शहद और तैल दोनों से, क्षार से और लवण से भी। यह बस्ति कफ-व्याधियों में, पाण्डु-रोग यानी फीकेपन वाली रक्ताल्पता में और विसूची यानी उलटी-दस्त वाली तीव्र बीमारी में उपयुक्त है।
english: With fruits, with honey and oil (both), with kṣāra and with salt (lavaṇa). The enema (basti) is suitable in Kapha disorders, in pāṇḍu disease (anaemia with pallor) and in visūcī (acute vomiting and purging, a cholera-like illness).
notes:
line 05.05.20: Printed 'ḻ' in saphaḻaiḥ is read as ordinary l (print variant). Continues 18-19 (instrumentals of added substances); no verb here.
line 05.05.21: The sentence continues in 22. 'yuktaḥ' is taken as 'suitable' (literally 'joined, applied'). Identifications: pāṇḍuroga = anaemia with pallor (standard); visūcī = acute vomiting and purging, cholera-like (probable). 'kaphavyādhi' read as a disorder of Kapha.

words.gloss: amṛtā (guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia; standard); the printed word is broken across the token break
(completes amṛta; sandhi a+e gives ai in -mṛtairaṇḍa)

hindi: शुक्र और अनिल यानी वायु की रुकावटों में तथा बस्ति के आटोप यानी गुड़गुड़ाहट वाले फूलाव में यह प्रशंसित है। मुस्ता यानी नागरमोथा, पाठा, अमृता यानी गिलोय, एरण्ड यानी अरंडी, बला यानी सम्भवतः बरियार, रास्ना और पुनर्नवा।
english: In obstructions of semen and of wind (anila), and in āṭopa (rumbling distension) of the bladder region (basti), it is esteemed. Musta (nut-grass), pāṭhā, amṛtā (guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia), eraṇḍa (castor), balā (probably Sida cordifolia), rāsnā and punarnavā (Boerhavia diffusa).

text_flags.why: possible: the printed space falls inside amṛta+eraṇḍa (amṛtairaṇḍa); the two tokens form one word

notes:
line 05.05.22: Continues 21. 'basti' in 'bastyāṭopa' is read as the bladder region, not the enema; 'āṭopa' = rumbling or distension (probable). 'anila' (wind) is the wind-humour or simply wind; kept as 'wind'.
line 05.05.23: A list with no verb; the drugs go with the preparation of 24-27. The token break inside 'amṛtairaṇḍa' is a print artefact. Identifications: musta = Cyperus rotundus (standard); amṛtā = Tinospora cordifolia (standard); balā = Sida cordifolia (probable); punarnavā = Boerhavia diffusa (standard); pāṭhā and rāsnā as in 19 and 15.

words.gloss: rohiṇī (unclear which drug: kaṭukā or harītakī; disputed)
of the weight of a pala
madana (emetic nut, Randia dumetorum; probable); set of eight

hindi: मंजिष्ठा यानी मंजीठ, आरग्वध यानी अमलतास, उशीर यानी खस, त्रायमाणा जिसकी पहचान में मतभेद है, तथा पंक्ति के अन्त के अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार अक्ष यानी सम्भवतः बहेड़ा और रोहिणी जिसकी पहचान अस्पष्ट है। छोटा पंचमूल, एक पल के मान का, और आठ मदन यानी सम्भवतः मैनफल।
english: Mañjiṣṭhā (Indian madder), āragvadha (Indian laburnum), uśīra (vetiver), trāyamāṇā (identity disputed), akṣa and rohiṇī (on a conjectural reading of the end of the line: akṣa probably bibhītaka; which drug rohiṇī means is unclear). The lesser (kanīyaḥ) pañcamūla (group of five roots), of the weight of one pala, and eight madana (probably emetic nut, Randia dumetorum).
notes:
line 05.05.24: A list with no verb. The reading 'akṣa' + 'rohiṇī' is conjectural; the end of the line could also be one word. Identifications: mañjiṣṭhā = Rubia cordifolia (standard); āragvadha = Cassia fistula (standard); uśīra = Vetiveria zizanioides (standard); trāyamāṇā = disputed (Gentiana kurroo often given); akṣa = Terminalia bellirica (probable); rohiṇī = disputed (kaṭukā, kutki, or harītakī). Review: the printed avagraha in maṃjiṣṭhā'ragvadho is a print oddity (mañjiṣṭhā + āragvadha gives ā); the line is read as one dvandva compound, so ra-/u sandhi (āragvadha + uśīra -> -dhośīra) is internal.
line 05.05.25: 'kanīyaḥ pañcamūla' is the lesser five-root group (laghu pañcamūla); its members are not listed in the text. 'pālikam' ('of a pala') may apply to the pañcamūla alone or to all ingredients. madana = Randia dumetorum (probable). Continues 23-24. Review: kanīya (laghu) pañcamūla is the standard group śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī and gokṣura (standard reference tables; the text itself does not list them).

words.gloss: milk; two; prastha (a measure of volume); joined with

hindi: जल के एक आढक में उसे पकाए, चौथाई शेष रहने तक, और छाने। दो प्रस्थ दूध से युक्त उसे फिर पकाए, जब तक दूध शेष रहे।
english: One should cook that in an āḍhaka (a measure of volume) of water, with a quarter remaining, strained. Joined with two prasthas (a measure of volume) of milk, one should cook it again until the milk remains.
notes:
line 05.05.26: 'parisrutam' (literally 'flowed through') is read as 'strained'. Continues 23-25.
line 05.05.27: 'kṣīraśeṣam' read as 'until the milk alone remains' (the water having boiled away). The pronoun 'it' stands for the strained decoction of 26.

words.gloss: with a quarter in addition, i.e. one and a quarter (what is measured is not stated)
śyāmā (disputed; black turpeth is often given)
kara (unclear: not a known drug name; possibly karañja, conjectural)
with añjana (collyrium; the substance is not specified)

hindi: सपाद यानी एक और चौथाई जाङ्गल-रस के साथ, घी, शहद और सैन्धव सहित। पिसे हुए यष्टी यानी मुलेठी, मिशि यानी सम्भवतः सोया, श्यामा जिसकी पहचान में मतभेद है, कलिङ्ग यानी सम्भवतः कुटज का बीज, कर जो अस्पष्ट शब्द है और अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार लिया गया है, और अञ्जन के साथ।
english: With jāṅgala-rasa (the juice of dry-land animals) sapāda (one and a quarter; the unit is not stated), and with ghee, honey and rock salt (saindhava). With the ground (ones): yaṣṭī (licorice), miśi (probably dill), śyāmā (identity disputed), kaliṅga (probably kuṭaja seed), kara (an unclear word, on a conjectural reading) and añjana (collyrium).

english: The enema (basti), pleasantly warm, increases flesh, the digestive fire (agni), strength and semen. Vātāsṛk (wind-blood disorder, probably gout), meha (urinary disorder), fat (medas), arśas (haemorrhoids), gulma (abdominal lump) and retention of stool and urine.

english: It may destroy asṛgdara (abnormal menstrual bleeding), insanity (unmāda), swelling (śopha), cough (kāsa) and aśmakuṇḍala (an unclear word, on a conjectural reading). Good for the eyes, giver of sons, the king of the yāpanas (sustaining enemas), a rejuvenative (rasāyana).

hindi: प्रत्येक को अलग-अलग एक पल के अंश में गोक्षुर यानी गोखरू के बिना पंचमूल को पकाए। आढक दूध में, चार प्रस्थ, पिसे हुए यष्टि यानी मुलेठी आदि से युक्त।
english: One should cook the pañcamūla (the five roots) without gokṣura (small caltrops), each separately in a portion of one pala. In an āḍhaka of milk (a measure of volume), four prasthas (a measure of volume), joined with the ground (ones) beginning with licorice (yaṣṭi).
notes:
line 05.05.36: 'pṛthakpalāṃśam' is read as 'separately, in portions of a pala'. 'pañcamūlam agokṣuram' is the five-root group in which gokṣura is not included; which group is not stated here. gokṣura = Tribulus terrestris (standard).
OPEN (05.05.36) [minor] notes / agokṣuram: Needs a human: gokṣura belongs to the lesser pañcamūla (see 25) but not to the greater one, so 'pañcamūla without gokṣura' is either redundant (greater group) or leaves four roots (lesser group). Possible corruption (e.g. a different word for agokṣuram). Translation stays literal. Suggested: (no change)
line 05.05.37: Elliptic: the thing measured as 'four prasthas' is not named (the decoction of 36 carried over is the natural reading but not stated); no verb. 'yaṣṭyādi' = 'beginning with licorice'; the group is not listed here. Continues 36.

hindi: शहद, तैल, घी और सिन्धूत्थ यानी सैन्धव से युक्त बस्ति भलीभाँति प्रशंसित है। विशेष रूप से बच्चों, बूढ़ों, स्त्रियों, सुकुमारों और सुखी स्वभाव वालों के लिए।
english: The enema (basti), joined with honey, oil, ghee and sindhūttha (rock salt), is highly esteemed. Especially for children, the old, women, the delicate and those of a comfortable (sukha) nature.

english: Likewise, prepared with sahācara (probably prickly yellow barleria), balā (country mallow), sārivā (Indian sarsaparilla) and darbha (probably sacred kuśa grass). A milk enema (kṣīra-basti), likewise with abhīru (probably shatavari), guḍūcī (giloy) and the pair of bṛhatī.

english: Milk cooked with a paste (kalka) of māgadhikā (long pepper) and yaṣṭīmadhuka (licorice). The pañcamūla (five roots), those beginning with bṛhatī, each drug measured at one pala.

hindi: दो पल शालि यानी अगहनी चावल, गोधूम यानी गेहूँ, यव और माष यानी उड़द, यष्टिका यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी सहित। उनके साथ सिद्ध किया हुआ बकरी का दूध, कुक्कुट के अण्डे का रस और सिता यानी मिश्री।

english: The juice (rasa) of crab (kulīra) flesh, joined with the fluid of the eggs of the caṭaka (sparrow). With sugar (śarkarā), ghee and honey, the enema (basti) is considered the most aphrodisiac (vṛṣatama, 'most bull-like').

hindi: बकरे और सूअर से उत्पन्न अण्डकोशों यानी मुष्कों से तथा केकड़े और चटक यानी गौरैया के मांस से। दूध सिद्ध किया हुआ बकरे के मुष्क यानी अण्डकोश, उच्चटा और इक्षुरक यानी सम्भवतः तालमखाना के साथ, तथा शहद।
english: With testes (muṣka) from the he-goat and the boar, and with the flesh of crab (kulīra) and sparrow (caṭaka). Milk cooked with the testis of a he-goat, uccaṭā (a plant, not identified) and ikṣuraka (probably kokilākṣa, Hygrophila spinosa), and honey.

hindi: ये, माक्षिक यानी शहद से संयुक्त, मनुष्य को अतिवृष यानी अत्यन्त पौरुषयुक्त बना देते हैं। और वे स्तम्भी यानी रोकने वाले, न अतियोग करते हैं और न अयोग।
english: These, joined with honey (mākṣika), make a man exceedingly potent (ativṛṣa, 'very bull-like'). And they, stambhin (checking, retaining), bring about neither excess (atiyoga) nor lack (ayoga).
notes:
line 05.05.56: 'mākṣika' = bee-honey (standard in this context; the same word also names a mineral, pyrite, in other places - not meant here, probable). 'ete' refers to the preparations just described.
line 05.05.57: The sense of 'stambhin' ('checking, stiffening, retaining') and the agent 'they' are not firm; the sentence may speak of the preparations of 56. 'nātiyogam na cāyogam' read as 'neither atiyoga nor ayoga'. Some readings take 'stambhinaḥ te ca' differently - not decided.

english: For the most part, nirūha enemas are scraping (lekhana) and sneha enemas (sneha-basti) are nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa). In the yāpana enemas there is both; therefore anuvāsana (oil enema) in them is not desired.
notes:

line 05.05.59: 'ubhayam' (both) is not defined by the line; it presumably refers to the two kinds of effect or enema of 58 (lekhana and bṛṃhaṇa), but the text does not say. 'yāpana' is kept as the technical name of a kind of enema. Verb 'is' implied.

words.gloss: spoiled, disordered; menstrual blood (ārtava); semen (śukra) — of those in whom these are spoiled
to be devised, to be prepared

hindi: जिनका आर्तव और शुक्र बिगड़ गया है, उनके लिए पुत्र देने वाला और रसायन। और इस प्रकार अन्य बस्तियाँ भी बनाई जानी चाहिए और अनेक प्रकार से पकाई जानी चाहिए।
english: For those whose menstrual blood (ārtava) and semen (śukra) are spoiled, a giver of sons and a rasāyana (rejuvenating tonic). And in this way other bastis (enemas) also are to be devised, and are to be cooked, in many ways.

text_flags.why: the printed 'śuqāṇām' (ka with a dot, no ra) is not a word; 'śukrāṇām' (gen. pl. of śukra) is clearly meant, and 'ārttava' is printed for ārtava

notes:
line 05.05.88: Elliptical (no verb, subject 'it' understood). 'rasāyana' is kept with a short gloss; it names the branch of rejuvenation, and here a rejuvenating remedy. Normalisation: doubled -rtt- written -rt- in 'ārtava'.
line 05.05.89: 'naikaśaḥ' = na + ekaśaḥ, literally 'not singly', i.e. in many ways. 'basti' here is the enema.

hindi: सम्भव होने पर सौ बार या हजार बार पकवाए। दोषों का नाश करने वाली स्नेहबस्तियाँ, परिहार सहित, कही जाएँगी।
english: One should have it cooked a hundred times or a thousand, when it is possible. Sneha-bastis (unctuous enemas) that destroy the doṣas will be described, together with their precautions (parīhāra).

text_flags.why: possible: long ī in 'parī-' is not the usual spelling of parihāra; sense unaffected

notes:
line 05.05.90: 'saṃbhave sati' is a locative absolute, 'there being possibility'. 'sahasram' is read with 'vārān' (a thousand times). The object (what is cooked) is not stated; the causative 'pācayet' is rendered 'should have cooked'.
line 05.05.91: 'parīhāra' = avoidance, precaution (things to avoid). 'vakṣyante' is the passive future, 'will be told'.

words.gloss: the group of ten roots (daśamūla; standard)
bhūtīka (disputed; sometimes a fragrant grass, not enriched here)

hindi: दशमूल यानी दस जड़ों का समूह, वरा यानी सम्भवतः त्रिफला, रास्ना यानी सम्भवतः रासन, अश्वगन्धा यानी असगन्ध और पुनर्नवा यानी गदहपूरना। गुडूची यानी गिलोय, एरण्ड यानी अरंडी, भूतीक, भार्गी यानी भारंगी, वृषक यानी सम्भवतः अडूसा और शिरीष।
english: The daśamūla (the group of ten roots), varā (probably triphalā), rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata), aśvagandhā (ashwagandha, Withania somnifera) and punarnavā (Boerhavia diffusa), Guḍūcī (giloy), eraṇḍa (castor), bhūtīka, bhārgī (Clerodendrum serratum), vṛṣaka (probably Justicia adhatoda) and śirīṣa (Albizia lebbeck),

text_flags.why: possible: (1) extra anusvāra in 'yaiṃraṃḍa' read as guḍūcy-airaṇḍa (airaṇḍa 'of castor'; guḍūcī+eraṇḍa would give -yeraṇḍa, not -yairaṇḍa); (2) 'śeriṣa' is not a known drug name, 'śirīṣa' fits (kept as 'possible'; śairīṣa is another conceivable base)

notes:
line 05.05.92: Ingredient list (accusative); the verb is not in this unit. Identifications: daśamūla = the traditional group of ten roots, usually bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, pāṭalā, gambhārī, śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, gokṣura (standard; the line itself does not list them); varā = triphalā in the nighaṇṭus (probable); rāsnā = Pluchea lanceolata (disputed; Alpinia galanga and orchids are also given); aśvagandhā = Withania somnifera (standard); punarnavā = Boerhavia diffusa (standard).
OPEN (05.05.92) [minor] gloss / daśamūla list in notes: The ten-root list sits in the notes of 92 only; fine as standard, but a glossary entry would let later units reuse it. Identifications checked: rāsnā, aśvagandhā, punarnavā, varā tags are sound. Suggested: glossary entry
line 05.05.93: One long compound (dvandva) of drug names, accusative. Identifications: guḍūcī = Tinospora cordifolia (standard); eraṇḍa/airaṇḍa = Ricinus communis (standard); bhūtīka = disputed (a fragrant grass such as bhūstṛṇa is often given), so no firm identification; bhārgī = Clerodendrum serratum (standard); vṛṣaka = vāsaka, Justicia adhatoda (probable); śirīṣa = Albizia lebbeck (standard). The split of 'guḍūcyaiṃraṃḍa…' is uncertain.
OPEN (05.05.93) [minor] confidence / whole unit: low is right: damaged long compound; identifications are kept off the uncertain items (bhūtīka). No change. Suggested: none

words.gloss: sahacara (probably Barleria prionitis; probable, colour varieties differ)
kola (probably jujube berry, Ziziphus jujuba; probable)

hindi: शतावरी, सहचर यानी सम्भवतः कटसरैया, काकनासा और जिसका भाग एक पल है। यव, माष यानी उड़द, अतसी यानी अलसी, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर और कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी, प्रसृत से मापे हुए।
english: Śatāvarī (Asparagus racemosus), sahacara (probably Barleria), kākanāsā, and (the one) having a pala as share. Yava (barley), māṣa (black gram), atasī (flax), kola (probably jujube berries) and kulattha (horse gram), measured by prasṛta.
notes:
line 05.05.94: Identifications: śatāvarī = Asparagus racemosus (standard); sahacara = Barleria prionitis (probable; other Barleria species, differing in flower colour, are also called sahacara); kākanāsā = disputed (several plants proposed), so only the name is kept. 'palāṃśika' = 'having a pala as share'; the noun it qualifies is not stated, and 'each' is not in the Sanskrit; it may qualify the whole list. The printed 'ḻ' (paḻa) is written 'l' (pala) in the split (orthographic normalisation, recorded here once).
line 05.05.95: Dvandva of five items, accusative plural. Identifications: yava = barley (standard); māṣa = Vigna mungo (standard); atasī = Linum usitatissimum (standard); kola = Ziziphus jujuba, the jujube berry (probable; kola is also a name of other things); kulattha = Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard). 'prasṛta' is a measure, the amount held in a cupped palm; 'each' is not in the Sanskrit. The accusatives of lines 05.05.92-95 lack a verb here; they are most probably the objects of 'vipācya' in line 05.05.96 (sentence running across units; no verse pairing claimed).

lines_deva: वहे विपाच्य तोयस्य द्रोणशेषेण तेन च
lines_iast: vahe vipācya toyasya droṇaśeṣeṇa tena ca
hindi: वह नामक माप के जल में पकाकर, एक द्रोण शेष रहने पर, और उससे। एक आढक तेल को पीसने योग्य, जीवनीय, पल से मापे हुओं के साथ पकाए।
english: Having boiled (it) in a vaha of water, with a droṇa remaining, and with that. One should cook an āḍhaka of oil with (ones) to be ground, the life-promoting (jīvanīya) (ones), measured by a pala.
notes:
line 05.05.96: Doubtful sense of 'vahe': taken as the measure vaha ('a vaha of water'), with the genitive 'toyasya'. The size of the vaha and droṇa is not worked out here. 'droṇaśeṣeṇa' = 'with a droṇa as remainder', i.e. boiled down until a droṇa is left. 'tena' (with that) refers to the resulting liquid, continued in the next unit; the object being boiled is not stated. The object of 'vipācya' is most probably the drug list of lines 05.05.92-95 (not stated here).
OPEN (05.05.96) [minor] notes / vaha / droṇa: Measures not worked out (known risk). Standard: droṇa = 4 āḍhaka (about 12 litres by the usual 1 āḍhaka = about 3 litres); the size of the vaha differs between texts (a multiple of the droṇa) and cannot be fixed from this line. Human decision whether to add numbers. Suggested: append note if wanted
line 05.05.97: The nouns are not stated, so '(ones)' is used. 'jīvanīya' is the traditional group of ten drugs (standard): jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī, madhuka; the line itself does not list them. 'with that' of the previous unit (the decoction) continues here; no verb is supplied beyond 'pacet'.

words.gloss: all; Vāta; disorder; dispelling (-nud, regular final -t)
of marsh-dwelling (ones), animals of marshy ground

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ppp. upa-√sādh, f. nom. sg.

hindi: यह अनुवासन कहलाता है, सब वातविकारों को दूर करने वाला। अनूपों की वसा, उसी प्रकार जीवनीयों से तैयार की गई।
english: This, called anuvāsana (unctuous retention enema), dispels all disorders of Vāta. The fat (vasā) of the marsh-dwelling (ones), prepared similarly with the jīvanīya (ones).
notes:
line 05.05.98: Name given in the line: 'anuvāsana'. 'anuvāsana' is the oil enema retained for a time (standard). The stem of the last member is -nud, -nut is its regular form at the end of the word.
line 05.05.99: Elliptical, no verb. 'ānūpa' = belonging to marshy (watery) country; the noun (animals) is not stated, so '(ones)'. 'jīvanīya' see line 05.05.97. 'tadvat' refers to the preparation of the previous unit.

hindi: शताह्वा यानी सोआ, यव, बिल्व यानी बेल और खट्टों से सिद्ध किया तेल, समीरण यानी वात में। सेंधा नमक से, जो अग्नि के रंग का हो, तपाया गया और वात को जीतने वाला घी।
english: Oil cooked with śatāhvā (dill), yava (barley), bilva (bael) and sour (ones), for wind (samīraṇa, that is Vāta). Ghee (ghṛta), heated with rock salt (saindhava) of fire colour, and conquering Vāta.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhṛtam' (held) gives no good sense after 'taptam'; 'ghṛtam' (ghee) fits the context of oils and ghees and the metre

notes:
line 05.05.100: Print convention: 'śatāvhā' is the printed form of śatāhvā (recorded here once for this and later units). 'amla' is read as 'sour (ones)' (unstated nouns); the sense could also be a single sour drug. 'samīraṇa' = wind, a name for Vāta (standard); the locative is read 'for/against wind'. Identifications: śatāhvā = Anethum sowa (standard); bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard).
OPEN (05.05.100) [minor] english / for wind: Locative 'samīraṇe' is literally 'in wind'; 'for' is interpretation. Owner decision (same for hindi 'में' which is literal). Suggested: none
line 05.05.101: The reading 'ghee' rests on the suggested correction (see text_flags); on the printed 'dhṛta' the sense would be 'held/kept'. 'agnivarṇa' = fire-coloured, i.e. red-hot or glowing; the line does not say how the salt is used beyond 'heated with'. 'anilajit' = conquering Vāta (anila = wind).
OPEN (05.05.101) [minor] notes / dhṛtam/ghṛtam: Conjecture accepted (Devanagari द्ध for घ is a likely misread; ghṛta fits oil-and-ghee context and 'anilajit'). Translation rests on it; consider adding 'on a conjectural reading' to the English. Suggested: none

lines_deva: जीवंतीं मदनं मेदां श्रावणीं मधुकं बळां
lines_iast: jīvaṃtīṃ madanaṃ medāṃ śrāvaṇīṃ madhukaṃ baḻāṃ

words.gloss: medā (disputed; one of the aṣṭavarga drugs, not enriched)
śatāhvā (dill; see line 05.05.100); ṛṣabhaka (a drug of the aṣṭavarga group; disputed, not enriched)

hindi: जीवन्ती यानी डोडी, मदन यानी मैनफल, मेदा, श्रावणी यानी सम्भवतः गोरखमुण्डी, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और बला यानी बरियार। शताह्वा यानी सोआ और ऋषभक, कृष्णा यानी सम्भवतः पिप्पली, काकनासा और शतावरी।
english: Jīvantī (Leptadenia reticulata), madana (emetic nut), medā, śrāvaṇī (probably Sphaeranthus indicus), madhuka (probably liquorice) and balā (Sida cordifolia), Śatāhvā (dill) and ṛṣabhaka, kṛṣṇā (probably pippalī, long pepper), kākanāsā and śatāvarī,
notes:
line 05.05.102: Ingredient list. Identifications: jīvantī = Leptadenia reticulata (standard); madana = Randia dumetorum (standard); medā = disputed (a tuber of the aṣṭavarga group, often replaced; no firm botanical name); śrāvaṇī = Sphaeranthus indicus (probable); madhuka = Glycyrrhiza glabra (probable; Madhuca longifolia is also called madhuka); balā = Sida cordifolia (standard). The printed 'ḻ' (baḻā) is written 'l'.
line 05.05.103: 'śatāvharṣabhakau' is read as śatāhva + ṛṣabhaka in a dual dvandva (a + ṛ = ar); the stem shows the short final -a as compound member. 'kṛṣṇā' (lit. black) is taken as pippalī, Piper longum (probable; the word has other meanings).

lines_deva: पिष्ट्वा तैलं घृतं क्षीरे साधयेत चतुर्गुणैः
lines_iast: piṣṭvā tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣīre sādhayeta caturguṇaiḥ

words.gloss: śaṭhī (probably Hedychium spicatum; probable, Curcuma zedoaria also given)

hindi: स्वगुप्ता यानी कौंच, क्षीरकाकोली, कर्कट नामक, शठी यानी सम्भवतः कपूरकचरी और वचा यानी बच। पीसकर तेल और घी को चौगुने दूध में पकाए।
english: Svaguptā (cowhage), kṣīrakākolī, (that) named karkaṭa, śaṭhī (probably Hedychium spicatum) and vacā (sweet flag), Having ground (them), one should cook oil (and) ghee in fourfold milk.

text_flags.why: possible: the instrumental plural does not agree with 'kṣīre' (locative singular); the parallel line 'kṣīre caturguṇe' in the next unit but two suggests 'caturguṇe'

text_flags.src: पिष्ट्वा तैलं घृतं क्षीरे साधयेत चतुर्गुणैः ॥
text_flags.why: proofread pass (typo?, error): साधयेत lacks final consonant; sandhi with च

notes:
line 05.05.104: 'karkaṭākhyā' = 'named karkaṭa' (crab); the drug usually meant is karkaṭaśṛṅgī, Pistacia integerrima galls (probable), but the line only says 'named karkaṭa'. kṣīrakākolī: disputed (Roscoea or Lilium species proposed). svaguptā = ātmaguptā, Mucuna pruriens (standard). vacā = Acorus calamus (standard).
line 05.05.105: Translation follows the suggested 'caturguṇe' (fourfold, in relation to the oil and ghee is not stated). On the printed instrumental plural the sense would be 'with fourfold (ones)'. 'tailam ghṛtam' read as two objects; the ground substances are not named in this unit.

words.gloss: strength; semen; fire (agni, the digestive fire); increasing

hindi: पोषण करने वाला, वात और पित्त का नाश करने वाला, बल, शुक्र और अग्नि को बढ़ाने वाला। रज और शुक्र के रोगों को दूर करने वाला, और पुत्रीय यानी पुत्र से सम्बन्धित अनुवासन।
english: Nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa), destroying Vāta and Pitta, increasing strength, semen (śukra) and the fire (agni, the digestive fire). Removing ailments of menstrual blood (rajas) and semen (śukra), and the putrīya (son-related) anuvāsana.
notes:
line 05.05.106: Elliptical (no verb). Orthographic: printed 'varddhana' written vardhana. 'agni' = the digestive fire, as is usual in such lists; the line says only 'fire'.
line 05.05.107: 'putrīya' = 'relating to/for a son'; it seems to be a name of this anuvāsana, but the line does not say how it is meant, so it is kept literal. 'raja(s)' is taken as menstrual blood here (standard in this setting). Elliptical, no verb.

words.gloss: cold; touch; potency (vīrya) — (ones) of cold touch and potency
oil; quarter — having oil as a quarter

hindi: शीतल स्पर्श और वीर्य वालों से, और पिसे हुओं से, चौगुने दूध में। जिसमें तेल चौथाई है, ऐसा पकाया गया घी, पित्त का नाश करने वाला अनुवासन।
english: And with (ones) of cold touch and potency (vīrya), ground, in fourfold milk. Ghee cooked with oil as a quarter, an anuvāsana that destroys Pitta.
notes:
line 05.05.108: Unstated nouns (drugs) are shown as '(ones)'. 'śiśira-sparśa-vīrya' can be read 'cold in touch and in potency' or 'having cold touch and (cold) potency'; 'śiśira' is taken with both. No verb in this unit.
line 05.05.109: 'tailapāda' = having oil as one quarter (of the ghee, as is understood; the line does not say of what). No verb.

lines_deva: सैंधवं मदनं कुष्ठं शताव्हा निचलो वचा
lines_iast: saiṃdhavaṃ madanaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ śatāvhā nicalo vacā

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (the drug kuṣṭha, costus, Saussurea costus; standard)
nicula (disputed: Barringtonia or a cane; not enriched)
together with; kaṭphala (box myrtle, Myrica esculenta; standard)

hindi: सेंधा नमक, मदन, कुष्ठ नामक औषध यानी कूठ, शताह्वा यानी सोआ, निचुल और वचा। ह्रीबेर यानी सुगन्धबाला, मधुक, भार्गी, देवदार और कायफल सहित।
english: Rock salt (saindhava), madana, kuṣṭha (the drug costus), śatāhvā (dill), nicula and vacā (sweet flag), Hrīvera (Pavonia odorata), madhuka, bhārgī, devadāru (deodar cedar), together with kaṭphala (Myrica esculenta).

text_flags.why: possible: 'nicala' (motionless) is not a drug name here; 'nicula' is a known drug (Barringtonia acutangula or a cane) and fits a list of drugs
orthographic: ba for va (hrībera is an attested variant spelling); read as hrīvera

notes:
line 05.05.110: List in the nominative (neuter nominative equals accusative). 'nicala' vs 'nicula' is doubtful, so no identification is added; nicula is disputed (Barringtonia acutangula, hijjala, or Calamus, vetasa). Here kuṣṭha is the drug, not the skin disease; costus (Saussurea costus) is standard.
OPEN (05.05.110) [minor] text_flags / nicalo: Plausible; kuṣṭha as costus drug and nicula disputed: fine. No change. Suggested: none
line 05.05.111: Orthographic: printed 'hrībera' (ba for va), normalised to hrīvera. hrīvera = Pavonia odorata (standard; often given as balā-type fragrant root); devadāru = Cedrus deodara (standard); kaṭphala = Myrica esculenta (standard). 'sakaṭphalam' is 'with kaṭphala'.

lines_deva: नागरं पुष्करं मेदा चविका चित्रकः शठी
lines_iast: nāgaraṃ puṣkaraṃ medā cavikā citrakaḥ śaṭhī

words.gloss: puṣkara (probably puṣkaramūla, Inula racemosa; probable, the lotus is also meant by the word)
viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes; standard); ativiṣā (Aconitum heterophyllum; standard)
śyāmā (disputed: black turpeth or another plant; not enriched)
hareṇu (disputed, a seed drug; not enriched)

hindi: नागर यानी सोंठ, पुष्कर यानी सम्भवतः पुष्करमूल, मेदा, चविका यानी सम्भवतः चव्य, चित्रक यानी चीता और शठी। विडंग और अतिविषा यानी अतीस, श्यामा, हरेणु, नीलिनी यानी नील और स्थिरा यानी सम्भवतः शालपर्णी।
english: Nāgara (dry ginger), puṣkara (probably puṣkaramūla, Inula racemosa), medā, cavikā (probably Piper chaba), citraka (Plumbago zeylanica) and śaṭhī. Viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes) and ativiṣā (Aconitum heterophyllum), śyāmā, hareṇu, nīlinī (indigo) and sthirā (probably śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum),
notes:
line 05.05.112: List in the nominative. nāgara = dried ginger (standard); puṣkara = puṣkaramūla, Inula racemosa (probable; it is also a word for lotus); cavikā = Piper chaba/retrofractum (probable); citraka = Plumbago zeylanica (standard).
line 05.05.113: 'viḍaṅgātiviṣe' is read as a dual dvandva 'viḍaṅga and ativiṣā'. Identifications: viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes (standard); ativiṣā = Aconitum heterophyllum (standard); śyāmā = disputed (trivṛt variety, Ichnocarpus and others); hareṇu = disputed (renukā, seeds of Vitex or Piper species); nīlinī = Indigofera tinctoria (standard); sthirā = śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum (probable). The word viḍa (salt) of the glossary is not used here.

lines_deva: बिल्वाजमोदे चपला दंती रास्ना च तैः समैः
lines_iast: bilvājamode capalā daṃtī rāsnā ca taiḥ samaiḥ

words.gloss: bilva (see line 05.05.100); ajamodā (probably Trachyspermum roxburghianum, celery-seed type; probable)
capalā (a name of pippalī, long pepper, in some lists; disputed)

hindi: बिल्व और अजमोदा यानी सम्भवतः अजमोद, चपला, दन्ती यानी जंगली जमालगोटा और रास्ना, उन समानों के साथ। एरण्ड का तेल यानी अरंडी का तेल तैयार किया जाए, या तेल; कफ के रोगों को दूर करने वाला।
english: Bilva and ajamodā (probably celery-seed type, Trachyspermum roxburghianum), capalā, dantī (Baliospermum montanum) and rāsnā, with those, equal (ones). Castor oil (airaṇḍa-taila) is to be prepared, or oil, removing diseases of Kapha.
notes:
line 05.05.114: 'taiḥ samaiḥ' = with those, equal (ones): the sense is probably 'in equal parts', but 'parts' is not in the Sanskrit. 'bilvājamode' read as a dual dvandva. capalā: in some lists a name of pippalī; disputed, so left unenriched in the translation. ajamodā = Trachyspermum roxburghianum (probable). dantī = Baliospermum montanum (standard).
line 05.05.115: Read as 'castor oil is to be prepared (cooked), or (another) oil'; with what it is cooked is not said (the ingredients of the preceding units). 'kapharoga' = disease of Kapha. airaṇḍa = Ricinus communis (standard; also noted in line 05.05.93).

words.gloss: vardhma (scrotal swelling, probably hernia or hydrocele; probable)
udāvarta (reversal of the downward movement of wind and wastes; standard)
ānāha (distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind)

hindi: वर्ध्म यानी सम्भवतः अण्डवृद्धि, उदावर्त यानी वायु का उलटी दिशा में जाना, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, अर्श यानी बवासीर, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली का रोग और मेह यानी मूत्र के रोग, वात सहित। आनाह यानी पेट का फूलना और मल-वायु का रुकना, और अश्मरी यानी पथरी, इन्हें वह अनुवासन शीघ्र नष्ट कर दे।
english: Vardhma (probably enlargement of the scrotum, hernia or hydrocele), udāvarta (reversed movement of wind), gulma (abdominal lump), arśas (haemorrhoids), plīha (spleen disorder) and meha (urinary disorders), together with wind (māruta), That anuvāsana would quickly destroy ānāha (distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind) and aśmarī (urinary stone).
notes:
line 05.05.116: The accusative objects; their verb 'hanyāt' stands in the next unit. Orthographic: printed 'udāvartta' written udāvarta. Identifications: arśas = haemorrhoids (standard); vardhma = enlargement of the scrotum, hernia or hydrocele (probable); udāvarta = upward movement of wind (standard); gulma = abdominal lump (standard); plīha = disorder of the spleen (standard); meha = the group of urinary disorders (prameha); whether diabetes is included is not settled here. 'samārutān' = 'together with māruta (wind)'.
OPEN (05.05.116) [minor] gloss / meha: HUMAN DECISION: meha is the prameha group (twenty urinary disorders, classically including diabetes, madhumeha). 'urinary disorders' is safe; owner policy (modern names wanted) vs glossary OPEN on madhumeha. Not patched. Suggested: decide
line 05.05.117: Continues the sentence of the previous unit: 'hanyāt' takes the accusatives listed in the unit before. 'anuvāsana' see line 05.05.98. aśmarī = urinary calculus (standard); ānāha = distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind (standard).

words.gloss: five; roots; pañcamūla = a group of five roots (the five roots are not named in this unit)
bilva (Aegle marmelos, bael; standard); beginning with, and the rest

hindi: पञ्चमूल से साधित तैल, अथवा बिल्व यानी बेल आदि से साधित। अनुवासन श्लेष्म को हरने वाला, अथवा कफ का नाश करने वाले द्रव्यों से।
english: Oil prepared with the five roots (pañcamūla), or with bilva (bael) and the rest. An anuvāsana (oil enema) that removes phlegm (śleṣman), or one with substances that destroy Kapha.
notes:
line 05.05.118: Elliptical: 'sādhitam' (prepared) is read with both instruments 'pañcamūlena' and 'bilvādinā'. bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard); the Hindi name is bel. 'bilvādi' is read literally as 'bilva and the rest' without naming the members. Which oil and which enema it serves is not stated here (compare 119).
line 05.05.119: Elliptical: no verb is given; the line states what kind of anuvāsana (or with what substances) is meant. 'dravyaiḥ ... kaphaghātibhiḥ' is an instrumental 'with Kapha-destroying substances'. anuvāsana is the oil (unctuous) enema (standard).

hindi: कफ में फलों के साथ और आठ गुने खट्टे में पकाया हुआ अन्वासन। शूल और आनाह में उससे युक्त निरूह, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार सम्भवतः पटु यानी नमक और मूत्र वाला।
english: In Kapha, an anvāsana (oil enema) cooked with fruits and in the eightfold sour (amla). In pain (śūla) and distension (ānāha), a nirūha (decoction enema) joined with that, on a conjectural reading having paṭu (probably salt) and urine.

text_flags.why: possible: 'paiṭu' is not a word; 'paṭu' (salt, probable) with mūtra (urine) fits the sense of a nirūha

notes:
line 05.05.120: 'aṣṭaguṇe amle' is rendered literally 'in the eightfold sour'; the noun to which 'sour' belongs (a liquid?) and what is eightfold (the measure?) are not stated. 'anvāsana' is a variant spelling of anuvāsana (see 119). The line is a phrase without a main verb.
line 05.05.121: 'paiṭumūtravān' is not a known word; read as 'paṭu-mūtra-vān' (possible typo, ai for a). paṭu in drug lists is often salt (probable), but this is not firm. 'tadyukta' = joined with that, referring back to the preceding unit's anvāsana (reference not certain). nirūha = decoction enema (standard). Verb not given.

lines_deva: पृच्छतिस्म मुनिमित्यथ धीमानग्निवेश इह किं तु फलानां
बस्तिकर्मणि हितं सततं स्यात्तं पुनर्वसुरिति प्रशशास
lines_iast: pṛcchatisma munimityatha dhīmānagniveśa iha kiṃ tu phalānāṃ
bastikarmaṇi hitaṃ satataṃ syāttaṃ punarvasuriti praśaśāsa
hindi: तब बुद्धिमान् अग्निवेश ने मुनि से इस प्रकार पूछा: यहाँ, परन्तु, फलों में क्या बस्तिकर्म में सदा हितकर क्या होगा? उसको पुनर्वसु ने इस प्रकार उपदेश दिया।
english: Then the wise Agniveśa asked the sage thus: 'Here, but what, of fruits' '... may be always beneficial in basti-action (enema procedure)?' Punarvasu thus instructed him.
notes:
line 05.05.122: GROUPING: the question continues in 123 ('... may be always beneficial in basti-action?'). 'pṛcchati sma' is the present with sma, giving a past sense. 'iti' here (after munim) is read as 'thus', introducing the question; the question ends at 'syāt' in 123, and the 'iti' after punarvasuḥ in 123 goes with praśaśāsa. 'agniveśa' = agniveśaḥ (visarga dropped before iha).
line 05.05.123: GROUPING: completes the question begun in 122. 'taṃ' = him (Agniveśa, from 122). The sage of 122 is named Punarvasu here. 'iti' is placed after 'punarvasuḥ' and read as 'thus'; the answer follows in 124 onward.

lines_deva: कुटजस्य फलं हृदामये प्रवरं कौटफलं तु पांडुषु
lines_iast: kuṭajasya phalaṃ hṛdāmaye pravaraṃ kauṭaphalaṃ tu pāṃḍuṣu

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (a group of skin diseases; standard); beneficial
ikṣvāku (probably bitter bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria; probable); fruit
for those with prameha (a group of urinary disorders; standard)
in pāṇḍu (pale-disease: anaemia with pallor; standard)

hindi: यहाँ, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, गैरागिरी कुष्ठ में हितकर है; प्रमेह वालों के लिए सम्भवतः कड़वी लौकी यानी इक्ष्वाकु का फल हितकर है। कुटज यानी कुड़ा का फल हृदय के रोग में श्रेष्ठ है, पर कौट फल पाण्डु यानी रक्ताल्पता में।
english: Here, on a conjectural reading, gairāgirī (an unclear word) is beneficial in kuṣṭha; for those with prameha the fruit of ikṣvāku (probably bitter bottle gourd) is beneficial. The fruit of kuṭaja (kurchi) is foremost in heart ailment, but the kauṭa-fruit in pāṇḍu (anaemia with pallor).
notes:
line 05.05.124: 'gairāgirī' is not a known name; kept unsplit and unidentified (unidentified). Its femininity is shown by 'hitā'. ikṣvāku = bitter bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria (not Momordica; probable). kuṣṭha is read as the skin-disease group, not the drug costus, because 'hitā' goes with a disease context. prameha is rendered as a Sanskrit term (group of urinary disorders, standard).
OPEN (05.05.124) [minor] hindi / कुष्ठ / प्रमेह: No modern name beside the disease terms in Hindi (English has them). Hindi should read e.g. कुष्ठ यानी त्वचा रोग, प्रमेह यानी मधुमेह-जैसे मूत्र रोग (owner wording OPEN for prameha). Suggested: Owner decision on Hindi wording
line 05.05.125: 'pravaram' is carried over to the second half. 'kauṭaphala' is not identified (unidentified): it may mean 'fruit of kuṭa' or a corrupted form, so it is kept as printed. kuṭaja = Holarrhena antidysenterica (standard).

lines_deva: उदरे कृतवेधनं हितं मदनं सर्वगदाविरोधि तु
lines_iast: udare kṛtavedhanaṃ hitaṃ madanaṃ sarvagadāvirodhi tu

words.gloss: kṛtavedhana (probably ridge gourd, Luffa acutangula; probable)

hindi: उदर में कृतवेधन यानी सम्भवतः तोरई हितकर है; मदन यानी मैनफल तो सब रोगों में अविरोधी है। मधुर, कसैले और कड़वे के साथ, वह रूखा नहीं, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार तीखे, उष्ण और चिपचिपे के साथ।
english: In the belly (udara) kṛtavedhana (probably ridge gourd) is beneficial; madana (emetic nut), however, is not opposed to any disease. Sweet, with astringent and bitter (ones); that is not dry; on a conjectural reading, with pungent, hot and slimy (ones).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ṭṛṣṇa' (thirst) does not fit a list of qualities; sa-kaṭu-uṣṇa-picchila (pungent, hot, slimy) fits

notes:
line 05.05.126: udara is rendered 'belly' per the book glossary; in this context the disease called udara (abdominal enlargement) may be meant. kṛtavedhana is probably Luffa acutangula (probable); madana = Randia dumetorum (standard). 'sarvagadāvirodhi' = 'not opposed to all diseases' (not contrary in any).
OPEN (05.05.126) [minor] english / In the belly (udara): HUMAN DECISION: in a list of disease-specific uses (kuṣṭha, prameha, hṛdāmaya, pāṇḍu, udara) 'udare' is almost certainly the disease udara (abdominal enlargement/ascites-type; standard). GLOSSARY says udara = belly (not ailment); OPEN_ITEMS already lists this as an owner decision (ch05 u107). Left unpatched. Suggested: In udara (the belly disease)
line 05.05.127: Subject is madana of 126 (understood). 'sakaṭṛṣṇapicchilaṃ' is printed with 'ṭṛṣṇa' ('thirst'); read as sa-kaṭu-uṣṇa-picchila on a conjectural reading (possible typo: ṭū for ṭṛ). 'kaṣāya' here is the astringent taste.

words.gloss: wind (pavana); going in the natural direction

hindi: जो कफ और पित्त को हरने वाला, शीघ्र काम करने वाला, हानिरहित और वायु का अनुलोमन करने वाला है। इसलिए वह फल आदि में आस्थापन के प्रयोगों में श्रेष्ठ माना गया है।
english: Which removes Kapha and Pitta, acts quickly, is harmless, and makes the wind (pavana) move in its natural direction (anuloma). Therefore that is held foremost among fruit and the rest, in applications of āsthāpana (decoction enema).
notes:
line 05.05.128: 'hṛdāśukāri' is split hṛt + āśukāri (hṛt becomes hṛd before ā). Alternative reading 'hṛd' (heart) is not supported by the sentence. Continues the description of madana (126-127).
line 05.05.129: Closes the answer of Punarvasu. 'phalādiṣu' = among fruit and the rest. āsthāpana is the decoction enema (= nirūha, standard). The closing 'iti' (thus) after yojanāsu is left out of the translations per glossary.

lines_deva: अथ मुनिवृषभे निगद्य वाक्यं स्थितवति विज्ञापयांबभूव भूयः
lines_iast: atha munivṛṣabhe nigadya vākyaṃ sthitavati vijñāpayāṃbabhūva bhūyaḥ

words.gram: past act. part. (-vat) √sthā, m. loc. sg.

hindi: तब मुनिश्रेष्ठ के वचन कहकर रुक जाने पर, उसने फिर निवेदन किया।
english: Then, when the bull among sages (muni-vṛṣabha) had spoken his words and stopped, he again made a request.
notes: The subject of 'vijñāpayāṃ babhūva' is not named in this unit; 131 gives the speaker as bowed down with the other disciples (Agniveśa by context, not stated). 'vijñāpayāṃbabhūva' is the periphrastic perfect 'vijñāpayām babhūva'. 'munivṛṣabha' is an epithet, here for Punarvasu by context.

words.gloss: gone down to the ground, bowed

hindi: यह अत्यन्त गहन; अन्य शिष्यों के साथ भूमि पर झुका हुआ, आगे अञ्जलि रखकर।
english: This very profound (matter): bowed down to the ground together with the other disciples, having placed the joined hands (añjali) in front.

text_flags.why: possible: 'jalim' is not a word; ñ was dropped in print, añjali (joined hands) intended

notes: GROUPING: the sentence is incomplete; it runs into 132 and 133, where the question is stated. The verb is not in this unit. 'idam' (this) is read as the object of the question that follows.

hindi: गुरु के द्वारा विचित्र कर्म और गुण करने वाला कहा गया बस्ति ऊपर जाता है, और नाभि से नहीं। और शीघ्र आता है, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार अनुस अस्पष्ट, देह से सब ओर से; दोषों को कैसे हटाता है।
english: The basti (enema), said by the teacher to produce varied actions and benefits, goes upward then, and not from the navel. And quickly arrives, 'anusa' (unclear), from the body on all sides; how does it drive away the doṣas?
notes:
line 05.05.132: The line is hard: 'ca eti na nābheḥ' is rendered literally ('and goes, not from the navel'); the intended contrast (it goes upward, yet it is applied below the navel) is not stated in the Sanskrit and is not added. 'guṇa' is taken as 'benefit, quality'. The question continues in 133. 'atha' could also be read as a sentence particle.
OPEN (05.05.132) [error] english / goes upward then, and not from the navel: LIKELY WRONG: ūrdhvam takes the ablative (nābheḥ) and means 'above the navel'; 'ūrdhvam eti na nābheḥ' most naturally = '(the basti) does not go above the navel'. This also fits 133, where the question is how a basti applied below can quickly clear doṣas from the whole body. The draft's 'goes upward ... and not from the navel' is ungrammatical sense. HUMAN DECISION; proposed English: 'The basti, said by the teacher to produce varied actions and benefits, then does not go above the navel' (literal order: atha ca eti, na ūrdhvam nābheḥ). Left unpatched; confidence stays low. Suggested: See problem
line 05.05.133: GROUPING: completes the question begun in 131-132; the teacher answers from 134. 'cānusa' cannot be restored with certainty (perhaps a sandhi/typo for a word like 'anusṛtya'); kept as printed and glossed unclear; reading is conjectural. 'apohati' is from apa-√ūh (drives away, removes).
OPEN (05.05.133) [minor] text_flags / cānusa: Unrestorable word is only in notes (with a speculative 'anusṛtya'); consider a text_flag with an empty suggest. Metre: the line is 22 syllables with cānusa counted as 3, so a three-syllable word is expected. Suggested: Optional flag

hindi: गुरु ने कहा: यह शरीर का, जो बाहर या भीतर आश्रित है, स्तिमित वायु के वश में है।
english: The teacher said: this of the body, whatever is dependent outside or within, is subject to the wind (māruta) that is stimita (still, stagnant).
notes: Difficult line. 'stimitamārutavaśyam' is read as 'subject to still (stagnant) wind'; 'stimita' may also mean 'wet, steady'. 'apāśritam' is read as 'dependent, resting'. The relative 'yat' and the demonstrative 'etat' are not fully resolved; this is a literal reading.

lines_deva: दुष्टस्य तस्य जनयन्ननुलोमतां तु बस्तिर्हिनस्ति विषमान्तिरोगपूगान्
lines_iast: duṣṭasya tasya janayannanulomatāṃ tu bastirhinasti viṣamāntirogapūgān

words.gram: pres. part. caus. √jan, m. nom. sg.

words.gloss: unclear (printed form kept); ends in roga-pūgān 'crowds of diseases'

hindi: उस दूषित के अनुलोम भाव को उत्पन्न करता हुआ बस्ति, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार अस्पष्ट विषमान्तिरोगपूगान् को नष्ट करता है।
english: Producing the natural direction (anulomatā) in that spoiled (wind), the basti destroys, on a conjectural reading, the 'viṣamāntirogapūgān' (unclear; the end of the word is 'groups of diseases').
notes: 'viṣamāntirogapūgān' is kept unsplit: the first part is damaged (perhaps viṣama-āntara-roga-pūga 'irregular internal groups of diseases', not firm). 'tasya duṣṭasya' is read as the wind of 134 (the wind that is stagnant); noun not stated.

lines_deva: ये संति तेषां न तु कश्चिदन्यो वायोः परं जन्मनि हेतुरस्ति
lines_iast: ye saṃti teṣāṃ na tu kaścidanyo vāyoḥ paraṃ janmani heturasti

words.gloss: vital spot (marma); upper; all; parts; limbs; born in

hindi: शाखा में गए और कोष्ठ में गए रोग, और मर्म, ऊर्ध्व, सब अवयवों और अंगों में उत्पन्न होने वाले। जो हैं, उनके जन्म में वायु से परे कोई और हेतु नहीं है।
english: Diseases gone to the branches (śākhā) and gone to the storehouse (koṣṭha), and those born in the vital spots (marma), the upper (parts), and all the parts and limbs. Those that exist: of them there is no other cause at all, beyond wind (vāyu), in (their) origin.
notes:
line 05.05.136: Continues in 137 ('ye santi teṣām'). The compound 'marma-ūrdhva-sarva-avayava-aṅga-ja' is read as a list of locations of origin. śākhā is rendered literally as 'branch'; koṣṭha as 'storehouse'.
line 05.05.137: Refers back to the diseases of 136. 'vāyoḥ param' is read as 'other than, beyond wind'.

lines_deva: तस्यातिवृद्धस्य शमायं नान्यद्वस्तेः समं भेषजमस्ति यस्मात्
lines_iast: tasyātivṛddhasya śamāyaṃ nānyadvasteḥ samaṃ bheṣajamasti yasmāt

words.gloss: faeces; drying, wasting (śoṣa); Pitta; and so on; waste (mala); accumulations

hindi: विट्, शोष, पित्त आदि मलों के संचयों का विक्षेप और संहार करने वाला वायु ही है। उस अत्यन्त बढ़े हुए के शमन के लिए बस्ति के समान दूसरा कोई औषध नहीं है, क्योंकि
english: For wind (vāyu) is the doer of the scattering and the gathering of the accumulations of wastes (mala): faeces, drying (śoṣa), Pitta and so on. For the pacification of that greatly increased (wind) there is no other remedy equal to basti, because

text_flags.why: possible: dative 'śamāya' (for pacification) fits; the final anusvara is a typo

notes:
line 05.05.138: The first compound is hard to divide: 'viṭ-śoṣa-pitta-ādi-mala-ācaya'; it is taken as the accumulations of faeces, śoṣa (drying/wasting), Pitta and other wastes. 'śoṣa' in a list with faeces and Pitta is odd (possible corruption, e.g. of 'śleṣma'); not changed.
OPEN (05.05.138) [minor] text_flags / viṭśoṣapittādimalācayānāṃ: The note itself suspects a corruption of 'śoṣa' (e.g. śleṣma) but text_flags is empty; an unflagged suspected typo needs a flag with 'possible'. No safe suggestion, so left to the owner. Suggested: Add flag: possible corruption of śoṣa
line 05.05.139: GROUPING: the 'because' clause continues in 140. 'basteḥ' is printed 'vasteḥ' (orthographic va for ba, normalised in `w`). 'śamāyaṃ' has a stray anusvara.
